fields.meta_title: Food Order Form Builder for Takeout and Catering | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a food order form for takeout, meal prep, office lunches, and catering that flags allergies and closes at your cutoff. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Food Order Form Your Kitchen Can Cook From
fields.hero_description: Build a food order form that puts allergies on the kitchen ticket, closes at your cutoff, and saves orders to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After the Customer Orders
fields.features_subheading: A food order form puts the dish and pickup time in one record, next to any allergy. These six parts carry that record to the cooks.
fields.feature_1:
Built from the menu you already use

Emergent builds the form from a plain-English description of your menu, with a price on every size and add-on. Ask for a Friday special later, and Emergent adds it to the form.
fields.feature_2:
Choices that follow the dish picked

Customers choose a dish, then its options one screen at a time, such as spice level or rice or noodles. The form shows only the add-ons that belong to the dish chosen.
fields.feature_3:
Every order saved as a row you own

Each order lands in a database you own, with the items and pickup time beside the phone number. When a regular calls for the usual, look up their last order and read it back.
fields.feature_4:
A kitchen screen that updates live

The app shows a live kitchen view sorted by pickup time. A new order appears on the screen the moment it is sent, and nobody at the stove has to check an inbox for it.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts where the owner already looks

The app sends a Slack message or an email when a catering order arrives or when the cutoff passes. Customers can get a reminder with their pickup time the day before.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours to keep

Export the complete code of the form and its kitchen view to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can take it over later, and the orders stay in your database.

fields.usecase_heading: One Form, Four Kinds of Food Orders
fields.tab_content_1:
The kitchen ticket leads with the peanut allergy

Juniper Street Noodle Bar sends every takeout order to a screen above the wok station. Callum Ferreira ordered 2 pad see ew for 6:45 pm pickup and ticked peanut on the allergy list. His ticket came up with the peanut allergy above the dishes, and the cook set out a clean wok before starting it.
fields.tab_content_2:
At 8 pm Thursday, ordering stops and the prep list goes out

Halvorsen Meal Prep plans the week around one number: meals to cook on Saturday for Sunday delivery. The menu takes orders until 8 pm Thursday, then closes. At 8 pm, chef Bea Lindqvist got the prep list by email: 42 chicken bowls, 31 lentil curries, and 19 salmon plates, 92 meals in all.
fields.tab_content_3:
One Slack message carries all 18 lunches

Lunch at Tidewater Survey Group used to arrive as texts to the office manager. Now staff pick from the deli menu on the form until 10:30 am. At 10:30, Marguerite Osei got one Slack direct message with all 18 orders: 7 turkey clubs, 6 falafel wraps, and 5 Cobb salads. She called the deli once.
fields.tab_content_4:
40 guests at $14 each come to $560 on the form

Cobblestone Catering quotes by the guest: $14 a guest for its taco bar, with a 20-guest minimum. Anika Brandt entered 40 guests for a retirement party. Before she sent the order, the form showed $560 and 4 trays of each filling, at 1 tray per 10 guests.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Food Order Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a food order form that gets complete orders to the kitchen before the cutoff.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write the menu as customers order
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick a cutoff you can prep against
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about allergies on every order
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide who hears about each order
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write the menu the way customers order from it: each dish with its sizes and add-ons, and a price beside every one. Group the add-ons under the dish they belong to, and leave out anything you make only on request.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick a cutoff you can shop and prep against. A takeout counter might stop taking orders 20 minutes before closing, and a weekly menu might close 2 days before the cooking starts. Write the time down with its weekday.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Make the allergy question part of the order itself, not a notes box at the end. A checklist with an Other line reads faster at the stove than free text. Decide where the answer sits on the kitchen ticket before you build.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Each person who handles an order needs a different signal. The line cooks may need only the live screen. The owner may want a Slack message for each catering order, and the chef one email with the totals once the cutoff passes.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Paste your notes into one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your notes from the first four steps into one prompt. Emergent builds the screens customers and cooks see, with the database behind them. Ask for changes the same way, such as a new special or a later Friday cutoff.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Share the link where customers look
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the form's link where customers already look for you: the menu page of your website and a printed QR code by the register. For an office lunch, post it in the staff chat at the same time each morning.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run a test rush with three orders: one plain, one with an allergy ticked, and one sent a minute after the cutoff. Check that the allergy shows at the top of the ticket and that the late order cannot go through.

faq_plan.q: What is a food order form?
faq_plan.a: A food order form is what a customer fills in to order food. It records the dishes and when they are wanted, plus anything the cook must know, such as an allergy. A takeout counter can run one, and so can a caterer or an office collecting lunch. Every submitted form becomes one order to cook from.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a food order form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: your menu with prices and the pickup times you offer, plus your cutoff. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. You change it by asking, for example to add a weekend brunch menu.

faq_plan.q: What should a restaurant order form include for takeout?
faq_plan.a: A restaurant order form for takeout should include each dish with its options and a pickup time chosen from slots. Ask for a name and phone number, and add an allergy question. Add one notes line for requests like extra sauce. Limit each pickup slot to the number of orders your line can cook in that window.

faq_plan.q: How do I take catering orders with a food order form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the event date and guest count, and have the form price the order per guest with a minimum. Once you accept a catering job, track it like a work order form: one record per event, with a status you move from confirmed to prepped to delivered.

faq_plan.q: How should a food order form ask about allergies?
faq_plan.a: Ask with a checklist on every order, plus an Other line for anything the list leaves out. The federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act defines the major food allergens as milk, egg, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, wheat, peanuts, soybeans, and sesame. Start the checklist with those, and show the answer at the top of the kitchen ticket.

faq_plan.q: Can a food order form add up the total as customers pick items?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give every dish and add-on a price, and the form adds them up as the customer chooses, with the total shown before the order is sent. Emergent builds the pricing logic from the menu you describe, per-guest rates and minimums included.

faq_plan.q: Can a food order form also take shirt orders for the same event?
faq_plan.a: Yes, but two forms work better. Food orders need pickup times and allergy answers, while shirts need sizes and colors and close on a different deadline. Put the shirts on a t shirt order form and link to it from the food form's confirmation page. Each list then stays clean for the person who fills it.

faq_plan.q: How do I set an order cutoff time on a food order form?
faq_plan.a: Pick the last moment you can still shop and prep, then give Emergent the day and time, such as 8 pm Thursday. The form stops taking orders at that time and reopens on the day you set. Show the cutoff at the top of the form, where a late customer sees it before filling anything in.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free food order form template?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a food order form. For a simple food order form, describe your menu in a sentence or two, then add pickup slots or allergy questions later. There is no response cap on the orders it collects.

faq_plan.q: How is a food order form different from a general order form?
faq_plan.a: The difference is time. A general order form sells products that ship or sit on a shelf, where quantity and address matter most. Food is ordered for a set hour. Its form also has to say when ordering closes and show the cook what matters first, such as allergies.

plan.angle: The top 10 for food order form is template galleries and printable sheets: a menu grid with quantity boxes and a name line. None shows what happens after the order is placed, which is where food sellers lose time: an allergy the cook never sees, orders that keep arriving after the shopping is done, a group lunch collected over 20 texts, and a catering quote worked out by hand. This page shows a food order form handling each of those for a takeout counter, a meal prep kitchen, an office lunch and a caterer, and the FAQ covers what a restaurant order form needs, allergies, cutoffs, totals, catering, free templates and how it differs from a general order form.
